---
title: "About"
---

**Intelligence Engineering** is a home for technical notes, experiments and practical explanations about contemporary machine intelligence.

The emphasis is not on following every new model release. It is on understanding the engineering choices that make models useful: adaptation, retrieval, evaluation, deployment, provenance and decision-making.

Topics will include:

- small and sovereign models;
- fine-tuning and model adaptation;
- summarisation and structured generation;
- retrieval-augmented generation;
- knowledge graphs and GraphRAG;
- evaluation, observability and provenance; and
- emerging decision models and agentic systems.

## A note on the articles

Articles will range from concise technical notes to more substantial, reproducible investigations. Dates show first publication; material changes should be recorded in an update note.

## About the author

I’m Martin Callaghan, an academic and technologist interested in the
practical engineering of machine intelligence. My work explores small and
sovereign models, retrieval, knowledge graphs, evaluation and the systems
needed to use models responsibly and effectively.

You can find the source for this site on
[GitHub](https://github.com/callaghanmt/intelligence-engineering).
